Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of Policy Document

## Economic Policy

The document outlines an economic strategy focused on fiscal responsibility, tax reduction, and business support. Key measures include reducing employee National Insurance contributions from 12% to 6% by April 2027, abolishing self-employed National Insurance by the end of the parliamentary term, and introducing a "Triple Lock Plus" for pensioners to ensure state pensions and tax-free allowances rise with inflation, earnings, or 2.5%.

The plan commits to maintaining fiscal rules requiring public debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP. Business support includes maintaining full expensing policies, not raising corporation tax, and providing £4.3 billion in business rates support over five years.

## Infrastructure and Transport

A £36 billion investment programme is proposed, redirected from cancelled rail projects, to fund local transport improvements including £8.3 billion for road maintenance, regional rail upgrades, and bus services. The plan includes completing existing rail projects, improving accessibility at 100 train stations, and supporting electric vehicle infrastructure.

## Immigration and Border Control

The document proposes introducing a legal cap on migration with annual parliamentary votes, removing illegal migrants through deportation programmes, and reforming asylum rules through international cooperation. Changes already implemented include raising salary thresholds for skilled worker visas and restricting dependant visas.

## Healthcare and Social Care

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors. Plans include expanding pharmacy services, building 250 GP surgeries, 50 Community Diagnostic Centres, and implementing a £3.4 billion technology investment programme. Mental health support would expand to all schools by 2030.

## Housing

A target of 1.6 million new homes is set, with measures including abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules, fast-tracking brownfield development, and maintaining stamp duty relief for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000. A new Help to Buy scheme would provide equity loans up to 20%.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in munitions production. The plan includes continued support for Ukraine, modernisation of armed forces, and maintaining the nuclear deterrent.

## Energy and Environment

The approach balances net zero commitments with energy security, including annual oil and gas licensing rounds, trebling offshore wind capacity, and building new nuclear capacity including Small Modular Reactors. Consumer protections include capping green levies and maintaining the energy price cap.

## Education and Skills

Proposals include protecting school funding, introducing mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (military or civic), creating 100,000 additional apprenticeships, and reforming 16-19 education through an "Advanced British Standard" combining academic and technical learning.

## Welfare Reform

Reforms aim to reduce working-age disability benefit spending through stricter assessments, tougher sanctions for those refusing suitable employment, and measures to combat benefit fraud. The plan projects £12 billion annual savings.

## Devolution and Union

The document commits to maintaining the United Kingdom's constitutional arrangements, protecting internal markets, and continuing direct investment in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland through various funding programmes.
